I traced every line: `controller.abort(new Error('late abort'))` at :373 fires no event on an already-aborted controller, and `pool.active` at :374 is unaffected by listener state, so reducing `#detach` (/home/user/fleet/pool/src/core/Pool.ts:235-240) to a no-op leaves the case green. No test in the package reads a listener tally. So the guide's claim at /home/user/fleet/pool/guides/pool.md:118 — "The listener is attached, recorded, and followed by an aborted-state recheck, then detached on every settlement" — has no gate.

Two corrections to the finder's diagnosis, both load-bearing for the repair. First, `createSignal` cannot observe this pool. /home/user/fleet/pool/node_modules/@orkestrel/test/dist/src/core/index.js:667-732 installs its counting `addEventListener`/`removeEventListener` as OWN properties on the created signal instance, while /home/user/fleet/pool/src/core/Pool.ts:125 registers through `AbortSignal.prototype.addEventListener.call(signal, 'abort', listener, { once: true })` and Pool.ts:238 removes the same way. Calling the prototype function with `this = signal` bypasses the own-property override entirely, so `count` stays 0 and the finder's instruction 'assert the tally is 1 while the acquire is parked' fails on the first run. Second, the abort path the finder targets cannot be pinned by any tally: Pool.ts:125 registers with `{ once: true }`, so when the listener fires the platform has already removed it, and the `#detach` at Pool.ts:222 is redundant for every abort a test can drive. rulings.evidence:
The quoted sentence is `.claude/rules/documentation.md` § Authority and workflow: "`guides/README.md` is the map: maintain both a concept index and a directory index. The concept index runs `spec ↔ source ↔ tests ↔ showcase` minus every column whose subject this workspace lacks." /home/user/fleet/pool/guides/README.md carries both: `## By concept` at :5-9 with the Concept, Spec, Source, and Tests columns for the one concept this package has, and `## By directory` at :11-15 mapping `src/core` to pool.md — and `src/core` is the package's only source environment. Nothing in that sentence, or anywhere in § Parity, obliges the map to describe a vendored mirror file sitting in the folder. The rule's only statement about mirrors is "A vendored dependency guide is a mirror... Refresh a mirror rather than rewriting it", which is about the mirror's own bytes.

The repair's precedent fails on its own terms. /home/user/fleet/queue/guides/README.md:17-33 names guide.md and scaffold.md under `## Vendored guides`, and :35-48 points at runtime dependencies by repository URL rather than at the local files — while /home/user/fleet/queue/guides holds abort.md, contract.md, database.md, emitter.md, timeout.md, test.md, and probe.md as well. Queue therefore names two of its nine non-own guide files, exactly the ratio the finding calls a defect in pool, which names emitter.md and guide.md of five. There is no fleet convention that a map explains every mirror in its folder, so the finding measures pool against a standard the cited precedent does not meet.
